newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says pilots strike would be disruptive.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says pilots strike would be disruptive.

text.p: President Clinton said Friday a pilots strike at American Airlines would be "quite disruptive" to air travel and urged the parties to reach out to each other.

"It cannot be a good thing for the people of the United States, and indeed people coming to the United States from other parts of the world, for a significant interruption to occur in the operations of this airline," Clinton told a news conference.

His comments came as he watched whether the two sides would be able to reach an agreement under federal mediators by a midnight Friday deadline. If they do not he could establish a Presidential Emergency Board and keep the pilots flying while attempts at compromise are made.

"We've had so many problems with our airlines for several years and now they've been doing quite well for the last couple of years. Our administration has worked very hard on that. This is an important part of America being seen as a vibrant, reliable, successful nation, and it would be quite disruptive if it occurs," Clinton said.

He reiterated his call to the parties to use the federal mediators and "think about how they can reach out to one another in the best interests of the nation, as well as of American and its employees -- all of its employees."
